items.laterWordingChange: CRRT-FELLOW-03 (2026-09-22), presentation only: the diagram label was “TMP = (FILTER + RETURN)/2 − EFFLUENT -18 mmHg”, which a learner read as an effluent of −18; the offset is now its own bracketed, signed term, and the current arithmetic is laid out beside the TMP readings. Expression, constant and calculation unchanged. Decision still NOT REVIEWED.
items.visual: Derivation label beside the filter on the simulated circuit, bracketed to the filter, return and effluent readouts.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: TMP has no sensor. It is calculated from three readings, and the fixed −18 mmHg term in the displayed expression is not an alarm limit.
items.supportingLocation: PrisMax Operator's Manual AW8035 Rev B JUN2019, program version 2.XX; manual p217 / PDF p218, section 'Transmembrane pressure and filter drop'. The printed expression is TMP = [(Pfil + Pret) / 2] − Peff − 18 mmHg.

sourceCheck.result: The expression is on PDF p218 exactly as registered and as implemented in engine/pressureModel.ts.
sourceCheck.notChecked: Whether later PrisMax software uses the same expression, and how the console labels the term.

items.hold: No hold on the expression itself. Currency is held under G01-CRRT-04.

items.topic: Filter pressure drop and the −25 mmHg correction

learnerSurfaces.locator: Filter pressure drop detail, 'Where it comes from' and 'What produces it'
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: Filter pressure minus return pressure. The PrisMax AW8035 manual says those two readings are corrected for a

learnerSurfaces.locator: Pressure-profile overlay: derivation label on the circuit diagram (correction bracketed as its own term, CRRT-FELLOW-03)
DEV-PM-010 record that learner citations resolve to (lesson source lists, evidence drawer, hub panel)
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: PrisMax presents filter pressure drop as filter minus return pressure and documents a sensor-height correction of the filter and return readings.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Constant applied to the simulated drop (calculation unchanged)

items.learnerWording: Where it comes from: “Nowhere. Filter pressure drop has no transducer of its own. It is calculated from the filter and return readings.” What produces it: “Filter pressure minus return pressure. The PrisMax AW8035 manual says those two readings are corrected for a -25 mmHg sensor-height bias; this simulation applies the -25 mmHg to the drop itself, which awaits device review. It describes how hard it is to push blood through the filter and the return limb.” Diagram label: “FILTER DROP = FILTER − RETURN + (−25 · IN REVIEW)”. Citation claim: “PrisMax presents filter pressure drop as filter minus return pressure and documents a sensor-height correction of the filter and return readings.”
items.laterWordingChange: CRRT-FELLOW-03 (2026-09-22), presentation only: the diagram label was “FILTER DROP = FILTER − RETURN -25 mmHg”; the correction is now its own bracketed term marked as in review, and the current arithmetic (filter − return, then the correction applied by this simulation) is laid out beside the filter-drop readings with the placement stated as awaiting device review. The −25 mmHg constant, where the simulation applies it, and the calculation are unchanged; the placement stays held (G01-CRRT-02 / O-04). Decision still NOT REVIEWED.
items.previousWording: Where it comes from: “… the difference between the filter and return readings, plus a fixed device display offset.” What produces it: “The device subtracts the return pressure from the filter pressure and applies a fixed display offset of -25 mmHg. …” Citation claim: “… a filter-to-return pressure relationship with a documented display correction.”
items.visual: Derivation label on the simulated circuit. The simulated drop readout is (raw filter − raw return) − 25 mmHg.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: Filter pressure drop has no sensor. It is calculated from the filter and return readings, rises with blood flow across unchanged resistance, and is watched for clotting or fouling.
items.supportingLocation: AW8035 manual pp201–202 / PDF pp202–203, section 'Filter pressure drop'. The printed expression is ∆Pfil = Pfil − Pret. The next paragraph states that the filter and return pressure readings are automatically corrected for a −25 mmHg hydrostatic bias caused by the sensors' different heights.

sourceCheck.result: The drop expression is printed with no −25 mmHg term, and the −25 mmHg correction is stated for the filter and return readings. The model instead applies −25 mmHg to the drop (engine/pressureModel.ts), taking inputs it names raw filter and return pressures.
sourceCheck.notChecked: Console behaviour. The Prismaflex manual (not available): record DEV-PF-005 describes a displayed, hydrostatically corrected drop there, which may be where the model's placement came from.

items.limitation: Program version 2.XX. Where the correction belongs is an interpretation until a device reviewer decides.
items.clinicalDecisionNeeded: PrisMax device educator, with manufacturer documentation if needed: on the console, does the displayed filter pressure drop equal displayed filter pressure minus displayed return pressure, or differ from it by 25 mmHg? Then keep the model, or change engine/pressureModel.ts, the derivation label and the pressure-profile numbers to match.
items.hold: Narrow hold on where the −25 mmHg correction is applied. Learner wording no longer attributes the model's placement to the manual. The simulated numbers, the diagram label and the tests that pin them are unchanged until the decision.
items.changeInThisBatch: Learner wording corrected in content/circuitModel.ts and content/foundationLessons.ts (G01-CRRT-03). Record text corrected in content/provenance.ts and content/phase7ReviewSources.ts. Engine comment corrected. Dated in the hub evidence panel. Calculation unchanged.

items.topic: Foundation teaching sentence stating both expressions

learnerSurfaces.locator: Foundation guided task on the pressure-sites tool (example normal-circuit-100), second teaching paragraph
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: For filter drop it prints filter − return and says the filter and return readings are corrected for a

items.learnerWording: “TMP and filter pressure drop are calculated from the monitored readings; neither has its own sensor. The PrisMax AW8035 manual prints TMP = (filter + return) / 2 − effluent -18 mmHg. For filter drop it prints filter − return and says the filter and return readings are corrected for a -25 mmHg sensor-height bias. This simulation applies that -25 mmHg to the drop itself; whether a console's displayed values follow that arithmetic awaits device review. Neither constant is an alarm threshold.”
items.previousWording: “TMP and filter pressure drop are calculated from the raw monitored readings. For the pinned PrisMax AW8035 profile, displayed TMP = (filter + return) / 2 − effluent -18 mmHg; displayed filter drop = filter − return -25 mmHg. These fixed device display offsets are not alarm thresholds. Neither calculated value has its own sensor.”
items.visual: Text beside the six pressure readouts in the guided task.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: Neither calculated pressure has its own sensor, and neither constant is an alarm threshold.
items.supportingLocation: As G01-CRRT-01 (PDF p218) and G01-CRRT-02 (PDF pp202–203).

sourceCheck.result: The previous sentence stated the filter-drop arithmetic as the manual's; the manual does not print it. The TMP part matched.

items.limitation: Program version 2.XX; the filter-drop sentence shares G01-CRRT-02's hold.
items.clinicalDecisionNeeded: As G01-CRRT-01 and -02, plus whether the added sentence about the simulation is clear enough for a novice.
items.changeInThisBatch: Wording corrected as shown. Constants and calculation unchanged.
